display.purpose: The Ascend wordmark on the login screen only.

title.purpose: A habit's name on its key.

title-list.purpose: A habit's name in the Habits list and History rows.

body.purpose: Buttons, fields and sentences; 16 px floor on inputs.

shadows.name: key-lip
shadows.purpose: The lip under a habit key at rest (accent-lip once done); 2 px when pressed.

shadows.name: button-lip
shadows.purpose: The lip under primary, secondary (surface-sunk) and danger (danger-lip) buttons; 1 px when pressed.

motion.name: motion-fast
motion.purpose: Answer to a tap; a cancelled hold shrinking back.

motion.name: motion-hold
motion.purpose: How long a hold takes; linear so progress reads as honest.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Quick to start, gentle to land.

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.purpose: Below it (phones, small windows) Today's date is always the short form; from it, the full date. In rem, so a larger browser text size counts as narrower. Everything else is fluid: rows wrap, columns stack by container queries.

components.name: Habit key
components.description: The signature: a full-width key you press and hold to complete a habit.
components.css: .ds-key{display:flex;flex-direction:column;justify-content:space-between;gap:12px;width:100%;min-height:96px;padding:20px;border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:24px;background:var(--surface);color:var(--ink);box-shadow:0 4px 0 var(--surface-sunk);font:inherit;text-align:left;transition:transform 150ms,box-shadow 150ms}.ds-key:active{transform:translateY(2px);box-shadow:0 2px 0 var(--surface-sunk)}.ds-key:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--accent);outline-offset:6px}.ds-key-top,.ds-key-foot{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;align-items:center;gap:12px}.ds-key-name{font-size:22px;font-weight:600;line-height:1.2}.ds-key-ring{width:32px;height:32px;border-radius:9999px;border:2px solid var(--ink-muted)}.ds-dots{display:flex;gap:6px}.ds-dots i{width:10px;height:10px;border-radius:9999px;background:var(--accent)}.ds-dots i.m{background:none;border:1.5px solid var(--ink-muted)}.ds-dots i.o{background:none;border:2px solid var(--accent)}.ds-key-streak{font-size:14px;font-weight:500;color:var(--ink-muted);font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums}

components.name: Primary button
components.description: The one main action on a screen: a persimmon pill on its own lip.

components.name: Secondary button
components.description: Header pills (History, Edit, Done) and quieter actions.

components.name: Danger button
components.description: Delete, only inside the inline confirmation; always with the trash icon.
components.html: <button class="ds-btn-danger"><svg width="18" height="18" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M4 7h16M10 11v6M14 11v6M6 7l1 12a2 2 0 0 0 2 2h6a2 2 0 0 0 2-2l1-12M9 7V4h6v3"/></svg>Delete</button>

components.name: Text field
components.description: A labelled box with a findable 3:1 edge; 16 px text.

components.name: Range switch
components.description: History's 7 / 30 / 90 days segmented control. Fixed radii (26 / 22 px), not full pills, so a two-line label at large text isn't cut by a circle.

components.name: Switch
components.description: A settings row (Settings, Feature 8): the label and a caption on the left, a 48 x 28 track on the right; persimmon when on. The whole row is the button (role switch); a failed save says so under it.

narrative.overview:
Ascend is a small, physical object on a sheet of bone paper. Every habit is a chunky key: it has a face, a lip along its bottom edge, and it sinks when you press it. Holding it down grows a persimmon tint out from under your finger; when the hold completes the key snaps to solid persimmon with a short pop. The whole system exists to make that one gesture feel honest and satisfying, and everything around the keys stays quiet so they can carry the screen.

The mood is tactile and warm, never clinical: warm paper and soft graphite instead of white and black, one persimmon accent instead of a rainbow of categories, one typeface (Bricolage Grotesque) whose optical sizes keep small labels calm and let titles show character. References are the feel of a mechanical keyboard key, Things 3's restraint (one accent, lots of air) and the bold type of Arc and Teenage Engineering product pages. It is a phone app first: a single 20 px-guttered column, big targets, thumb-height actions.

Copy is short, warm and never guilt-tripping ("Hold to complete", "3-day streak", "Start today").
keyCharacteristics: One accent, persimmon, reserved for "done" and the one main action on a screen.
Depth by a solid lip under the element, never by blur shadows.
Pills for buttons, 24 px keys for habits, 16 px for fields and cards.
Physical motion: things press down 2 px and spring back; nothing loops or moves on its own.
Dark mode is warm graphite with a lighter persimmon, and shows depth by lightness.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Persimmon means "done" or "the one thing to do now". A screen has at most one persimmon button; a secondary action that would compete steps back to the key-face style.

rules.name: The Tested Pair Rule
rules.body: Every text pair is 4.5:1 and every mark, edge and ring is 3:1, and `lib/palette.test.ts` proves it. A new pairing goes into `TEXT_PAIRS` or `NON_TEXT_PAIRS` before it goes on screen. Persimmon text never sits on the key lip (4.3:1 in light).

rules.name: The Token-Only Rule
rules.body: Components use the token classes (`bg-surface`, `text-ink-muted`, `shadow-[…var(--accent-lip)]`); Tailwind's own palette is switched off, so a raw colour can't sneak in.

rules.name: The 16 px Floor Rule
rules.body: Anything you type into is 16 px. Nothing that must be read is under 14 px.

rules.name: The 200% Rule
rules.body: Every screen still fits a 390 px phone with text at 200% (`e2e/text-size.e2e.ts`): rows that hold text and pills wrap (`flex-wrap`) rather than squeeze, and side-by-side groups use rem-sized columns so they stack when text grows.

rules.name: The Lip, Not Glow Rule
rules.body: Depth is a hard edge under the object in a darker shade of itself. No blur, no glow, no glass.

dos: Do keep 44 × 44 px as the smallest tap target, 48 px for main buttons.
Do put new colours in `app/globals.css` and `lib/palette.ts` together, with their pair in `lib/palette.test.ts`.
Do take every timing from `lib/motion.ts` / `--motion-*` (150, 200, 250, 650 ms) and wrap movement in `motion-safe:`.
Do give every filled button and key a lip in its own darker shade.
Do pair colour with a second signal: an icon for errors and delete, an edge for selected states, words for dots.
donts: Don't use purple gradients, glassmorphism, blurred drop shadows or glows.
Don't use emoji as icons; icons are simple 2 px stroke line drawings.
Don't nest a card inside a card; separate inside a card with a hairline.
Don't put grey text on grey, or persimmon text on the key lip.
Don't use a second typeface, or a font size under 14 px for text people read.
Don't round the Summit mark, or bring its sharp corners into screens.
